introduction: These are slides of Williams work.  They are his records, both used to show people what he made, as well as in lectures.  “The Arrowmaker” is Williams’ most famous piece.  Also, you can tell that the “Maid of Taos,” “Taos Girl and Deer,” and “Madonna” are all based off the woman from Bert Phillip’s patio/studio.
author: Jesse Ritner, PhD

introduction: This collection of lantern slides depicts three different towns: Taos, Taos Pueblo, and Red River City.  All three are on ancestral Taos land.  The three towns here demonstrate the variations on how people lived at the same time within a relatively local area.
author: Jesse Ritner, PhD

introduction: These lantern slides are all images of Williams.  The collection includes photos of him in his studio in New York City, as well as images of him dressed in costumes of “Mexicans” and of various Indian cultures.  For more information on dressing up as Indians please refer to my further readings page.
author: Jesse Ritner, PhD
